subject: Exec briefing: cross-team contingency & dependency snapshot
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Feb 2028 08:14:00 -0800
Subject: Exec briefing: cross-team contingency & dependency snapshot

Team —

Ahead of the QBR on Feb 21 I pulled together a concise snapshot of outstanding launch dependencies and the contingency options we'll propose to leadership. Attached is the high-level matrix (launch-readiness-matrix.xlsx). Key asks:

- Owners to confirm gating decisions by EOD Mon (2/13).
- Karthik: call out any infra or kernel risks that would push us beyond the current SLAs.
- Monica: note customer-facing timeline adjustments (if any) so we can align CS/AM messaging.
- Stephanie: please flag any customer escalation we should pre-brief (I suspect Acme has a procurement question about retention windows).

Quick summary from my side: two medium-high risks — (1) model quantization stability on long sequences, (2) the canary rollout doesn't hit preflight throughput on P100 pools. Both have mitigations but need owner sign-off.

I've left a one-page contingency plan in the sheet with three roll-forward options and an emergency rollback procedure. Please review and reply with confirmations or exceptions inline.

Thanks,
Priyom
Priyom Das
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: launch-readiness-matrix.xlsx (xlsx, 120KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Feb 2028 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Exec briefing: cross-team contingency & dependency snapshot

Priyom / all —

Thanks for the matrix. Quick tech readout:

- Quantization stability: we ran extended seq tests last night. On A100 the variance is within expected bounds. On older P100 nodes we see ~1.8% degradation on edge-case prompts (very long KV cache). Mitigation: short-term we can pin the hosted route to the A100 pool for high-risk customers (cost bump), mid-term we have a kernel patch scheduled in the dedicated pipeline (SUP-4821) that reduces degraded paths.

- Canary throughput: the issue is a misconfigured batch window in the autoscaler. We have a fix ready; will deploy to canary tomorrow morning (2/14 06:00 PST). If that doesn't hit target, contingency is to enable burst capacity for the first 48 hours (pre-approved cap: +15% spend).

I'll update the JIRA with exact SLAs and attach the perf logs.

-Karthik
Engineering Lead, Serving Runtime

Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 07:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Exec briefing: cross-team contingency & dependency snapshot

Looping in customer perspective: Acme's procurement pinged today asking whether retention can be reduced to 7 days for a pilot (their compliance team asked). That would materially reduce our KV cache blowup risk for their workload.

Proposed ask: Offer the 7-day pilot as a bounded workaround (7 days, non-production SLA, subject to review at 30 days). That gives us breathing room while Karthik's kernel work lands.

Also: we should prepare a short customer-facing note if we plan to pin Acme to the A100 pool — they will want cost/latency tradeoffs up front.

-Monica
Customer Success Manager

Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 11:16:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Exec briefing: cross-team contingency & dependency snapshot

Thanks — solid & pragmatic. Two executive asks before the QBR:

1) Priyom: include a one-slide decision table in the packet that shows the expected customer impact for each contingency (cost delta, latency delta, communications required).
2) Karthik: if the canary fix doesn't hit targets by 2/14 12:00 PST, prepare a short one-paragraph escalation for infra to approve burst capacity immediately. We need the pre-approval text in case we call it.

Also please capture the Acme retention pilot as a conditional mitigation; we don't want surprises in the QBR.

I'll be honest — if we can present a clear decision tree with owners and 'go/no-go' gates, the execs will be comfortable approving burst spend for 48 hours.

-Vivek
VP Product

- Karthik: canary fix deployed 2/14 06:00 PST. Early telemetry shows throughput within 95% of target; monitoring window open until 8:00 PST tomorrow.
- Monica: drafting the Acme pilot note (7-day retention) — will share the customer wording by 2/15 10:00 PST for approval.
- Stephanie: please queue the customer pre-brief; include the HubSpot note HS-987654 and route to Acme procurement if Monica signs off.
- I will prepare the one-slide decision table and put it in the shared Drive (link below) for the QBR packet.

Attachments: canary-rollout-plan.pdf (pdf, 48KB)

Thanks,
